prompt:
EDIT the supplied typography reference into a closely matched Chinese lettering study. The reference is the absolute visual authority. Preserve its delicate, quiet, airy architectural graphic-design character and its almost diagrammatic way of suggesting 3D space.

Create a clean white landscape artboard, without the surrounding black frame, browser UI, or descriptive labels. Main exact Chinese text: "精选作品集". Correct, recognizable five characters. Draw the words with the SAME VISUAL LANGUAGE as the reference "玻璃心": extremely thin charcoal hairline outlines, independent transparent geometric plane strips, parallelograms and triangles, selected stroke planes folded or intersecting at different depths, and a few very fine extended construction lines. Show all five characters on one generous line, with ample white space.

Important distinction: this is a FLAT GRAPHIC / architectural axonometric lettering drawing, like the supplied reference. Its depth comes from the intersections and orientation of thin, translucent planes. It is NOT a CGI render of solid 3D letters. No photorealistic light, no metal, no gemstones, no bevels, no glossy reflections, no thick extruded bodies, no glow, no floor, no cast spotlight, no dark background, no calligraphic curves or ornamental swashes.

The stroke system should feel specifically designed by a human: slightly unequal strip widths and heights; some open incomplete outlines; some strokes drawn only as fine lines; asymmetrical placement and subtly unexpected intersections inside each character. The irregularity is geometric decomposition and clever negative space, not arbitrary rotation or handwritten flourishes. Maintain clean structural intelligence and legibility.

Color: white body/front planes against a white ground, made legible through thin gray outlines and extremely pale cool-gray transparent fills (roughly 3–7% tint). A SMALL NUMBER of side-facing or crossing planes have an extremely pale diluted red/rose tint (roughly 8–14% opacity). Overlaps can be slightly deeper but always muted. The overall first impression must be almost white, ethereal and restrained, with a tiny breath of red. Do not use saturated red, red outlines everywhere, thick red shadows or gradients.

Aim for very close fidelity to the reference's hairline contour weight, sparse planar geometry, openness and lightness. Large clean margins. Main typography approximately 70% artboard width, moderate height. No extra text, symbols, decoration or watermark.
